title: Foundations
focus: The five moves everything else is built on. If these are not automatic, nothing later will be.

cards.title: Two Pointers
cards.trigger: Sorted input and you need a pair, or an in-place rearrangement where a write index can trail a read index.
cards.recall: Write the opposite-ends loop from memory. Then answer out loud: why is it safe to move `left` inward when the sum is too small, and what breaks if the array is not sorted?
useWhen: Sorted array, find a pair or triplet hitting a target
Remove or dedupe in place with O(1) extra space
Palindrome check from both ends
Cycle detection in a linked list (Floyd's)
Container / area problems where both walls matter
template: elif s < target:  left += 1     # only larger values can help
else:             right -= 1    # only smaller values can help
# Read / write: compact in place, keep relative order
keyInsights: Each pointer only ever moves one direction, so the loop is linear even though it looks nested
The sorted invariant is what makes discarding a whole side safe, that is the entire proof
Read/write is the same idea with both pointers moving forward at different speeds
cards.trap: The follow-up is 'what if there are duplicates and you must return unique triplets'. The answer is skip-while-equal after each accepted move, not a set at the end.

cards.title: Stack (LIFO)
cards.trigger: The thing you opened most recently is the thing you must close first.
cards.recall: Write the bracket matcher in six lines from memory. Then say why you compare against the expected opener on pop, and what the empty-at-end check actually proves.
useWhen: Bracket, tag or quote matching
Expression evaluation, postfix and infix
Nested decoding, one level pushes state for the level above
Undo and back-button history
Anything where you must postpone a decision until more input arrives
template: if not stack or stack.pop() != PAIRS[ch]:
return not stack        # nothing left open
# Nested state: push the frame, resolve on close
keyInsights: Two failure modes, not one: wrong closer, and leftover openers. Both must be checked
Guard with `not stack` before `stack.pop()` or you crash on a string that starts with a closer
For nested decoding, push the whole outer frame, never try to patch it in place
cards.trap: 'Now do it with a counter instead of a stack.' You can for one bracket type and cannot for three. Saying exactly why, you need unbounded nesting depth per type, is the answer they want.

cards.title: Binary Tree DFS
cards.trigger: The answer for a node depends on answers from its children, or on the path taken to reach it.
cards.recall: Write the postorder depth function without looking. Then answer the question that splits every tree problem in two: does this push information down the tree, or pull it up?
useWhen: Height, depth, diameter, any size-of-subtree measure (postorder)
Root-to-leaf paths and running sums (preorder, carry state down)
BST validation, inorder yields sorted order
Serialize and rebuild, preorder preserves shape
Anything answered by a single bottom-up sweep
template: # Postorder: pull answers UP from children
# Preorder: push state DOWN into children
if not node.left and not node.right:
# Iterative preorder when recursion depth is a risk
if n.right: stack.append(n.right)   # right first, so left pops first
keyInsights: Every tree DFS question is 'down or up'. Answer that first and the code writes itself
Space is O(h), not O(n). Say height, then say it degrades to O(n) on a skewed tree
Iterative preorder pushes right before left, that reversal is the only trick in it
cards.trap: 'What if the tree is a million nodes in a single chain?' Python recurses about 1000 deep by default. The expected answer is the explicit stack, not raising the recursion limit.

cards.title: Linear DP
cards.trigger: The answer at position i depends on a fixed number of earlier positions, and on nothing later.
cards.recall: Before revealing: state the recurrence in words, say what `dp[i]` actually means as an English sentence, and give both base cases. Naming the state correctly is ninety percent of DP.
useWhen: Count the ways to reach step or cell i
Best value ending at, or up to, index i
Take-or-skip decisions along a line
Any recursion with one integer argument and overlapping calls
Anything Fibonacci shaped
template: # 1. Define the state in one sentence, out loud:
#    dp[i] = number of distinct ways to reach step i
# Table form, when you need the whole history later
keyInsights: Say the state definition out loud before writing a line. If you cannot say it, you do not have the recurrence
Every linear DP that looks back a fixed distance collapses to rolling variables
Top-down memo and bottom-up table are the same recurrence, pick whichever base case is easier to state
cards.trap: 'Now you can climb 1, 2 or 3 steps, and step k is broken.' Both are one-line edits if your state is right, and a full rewrite if it is not.

cards.title: Grid DFS / BFS
cards.trigger: A 2D grid where connected cells form a region, and you are counting or measuring those regions.
cards.recall: Write the island counter from memory, bounds check included. Then answer: why does mutating the grid beat a separate visited set here, and when would it not?
useWhen: Count connected components in a grid
Largest or smallest region, perimeter, area
Reachability from a border, water flowing off a map
Fewest steps in an unweighted grid, which means BFS not DFS
Any implicit graph where neighbours are computed rather than stored
template: if r < 0 or r >= rows or c < 0 or c >= cols or grid[r][c] != '1':
# BFS variant: reach for this the moment the prompt says 'shortest' or 'minutes'
for _ in range(len(q)):           # drain one whole level per step
keyInsights: Bounds check first, value check second, and both inside the recursive call rather than before it
DFS answers 'how many' and 'how big'. BFS answers 'how far'. Choosing wrong costs you the problem
Mutating the grid is O(1) extra space but destroys the input, always say that trade out loud
cards.trap: 'The grid is a million by a million.' Recursive DFS blows the stack. Convert to an explicit stack or to BFS, and say it before they ask.
